reviewer: actual Claude, fresh blind session, no prior review context, no authorship
verdictBasis: Every promised vector was constructible and every constructed descriptor validates against the kit's own closed schemas, but five required findings remain: each is a place where two conforming implementations would disagree on admission or where a required public output has no expressible value. Any remaining MUST or SHOULD design gap requires CHANGES_REQUIRED.
scopeDisclaimer: This is a disposable design-reference exercise. It is not product qualification, not implementation authorization, and not a readiness grade. Every observation fed to my reconstruction (file bytes, closure trees, provider output, OS/compiler behaviour) is a synthetic assumption, never native enforcement proof.

inputCustody.note: The claimed parentSubjectSha256 is an assertion about a parent tree I was not given and therefore did not verify; I verified only that every listed file's exact bytes match its listed sha256 and byte length, that nothing is missing, and that nothing unlisted is present.

newMustIssues.title: The relation rung ladder is not carried by the registry the identity contract names as its source
selectors: docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/identity-and-evidence.md section 3, 'fact2 payload encoding: one explicit successor law': "its x-opensip-relation-registry carries each relation's selector, universe rule and rung ladder" and "resolution must be a rung of that relation's ladder"
docs/coop/design-corrections/foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-payload-registry/classes/relation ("fact.resolution must be a rung of the row ladder")
newMustIssues.observation: The successor registry has no `ladder` key at all. Its `rungs` member is a per-rung required/forbidden FIELD-RULE table and is the empty object {} for eight of the thirteen relations. Reading `rungs` as the ladder makes every `file`, `package`, `vcs-change`, `declares`, `literal`, `control-flow`, `reachability` and `clones` fact inadmissible, so no Run of the kind the contracts require could ever close. Reading the ladder from somewhere else contradicts the sentence that says this document carries it.
newMustIssues.whyItIsAMust: Two conforming implementations reach opposite admission decisions on the same bytes. The identity contract itself says an unresolved overlap of this kind is a design defect, never reviewer discretion.
newMustIssues.mitigatingFact: The values do exist in the kit and are unambiguous: docs/coop/design-corrections/native/capability-manifest-domains.v2.json#/registries/RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2/ladders publishes all thirteen ladders and they agree exactly with the inherited docs/coop/artifacts/fact-plane.v1.json#/relationRegistry/relations[].ladder. But that registry declares its boundPositions as `ProviderCapability.relations value` only, so it is not bound to fact2.resolution.
newMustIssues.requiredCorrection: Either add an explicit `ladder` array to each row of x-opensip-relation-registry, or make identity section 3 name RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2 as the ladder authority for fact2.resolution and widen that registry's boundPositions accordingly.
newMustIssues.reconstructionImpact: I proceeded under the stated assumption that the ladder is the inherited/RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2 value. Without that assumption none of the five Run graphs is constructible.

newMustIssues.title: `minResolution` carries two different closed vocabularies with no published mapping
selectors: docs/coop/design-corrections/workflows/schemas/policy-document.schema.json#/$defs/Resolution (enum: syntax, resolved, type, external) reached from #/$defs/Atom/properties/minResolution
docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/identity-and-evidence.md section 4 ("The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration, relation/rung, typed field filter...")
newMustIssues.observation: The evaluator must decide whether an admitted fact satisfies an atom's minimum resolution. The atom carries one of four abstract tiers; the fact carries one of fifteen ladder rungs; the native requirement record carries a rung. The two enums are disjoint (zero shared members). No document in the kit maps `syntax`/`resolved`/`type`/`external` onto ladder rungs, per relation or otherwise.
newMustIssues.whyItIsAMust: This is not algorithm freedom. Whether `minResolution: resolved` is satisfied by `resolved-target`, by `resolved-binding`, by `checked`, or by all of them is a public semantic decision that changes which findings a policy emits. Two conforming implementations produce different verdicts from the same Plan.
newMustIssues.requiredCorrection: Publish the per-relation mapping from the Atom `Resolution` tier to the relation's ladder rungs, or make Atom.minResolution a Rung and state the compatibility rule for existing policy documents.
newMustIssues.reconstructionImpact: My proof bundles use `minResolution: syntax` with an `exists` atom, where every candidate reading agrees. A policy needing `resolved` or `type` is not reconstructible.

newMustIssues.title: The `syntax-only` language mode has SUPPORTED-DESIGN fact cells but no admissible universe value
newMustIssues.observation: A `syntax-only` unit is contracted to produce declares/literal/control-flow facts at `syntactic` and clones facts at `normalized-body-hash`. fact2 and subject-scope both REQUIRE a universe h-identity, and the registered universe domain set has only TypeScript and Rust. There is no null branch, no third domain and no stated exemption. The same gap blocks `file`, `package` and `vcs-change` facts for any repository with no TypeScript or Rust unit at all.
newMustIssues.whyItIsAMust: A capability the matrix advertises as SUPPORTED-DESIGN is not representable in the identity graph. An implementer must either invent a third universe domain, invent a null branch on a required field, or silently narrow the matrix.
newMustIssues.requiredCorrection: Register a syntax-only semantic-universe domain with its own record and binding, or make the universe fields nullable with an explicit law for what a universe-free fact means, or state in the matrix that syntax-only cells produce no fact2.
newMustIssues.reconstructionImpact: I did not build a syntax-only Run; it is the one shape in the contracted matrix I could not construct without inventing design.

newMustIssues.title: `ScopeDocumentV1` is required to be an analysis-spec parameter, and the closed parameter registry has no row for it
selectors: docs/coop/design-corrections/workflows/schemas/comparison-result.schema.json#/$defs/EvaluationContext (description: scopeDigest is "raw SHA-256 of the canonical ScopeDocumentV1 bytes (the workflow glob scope-policy document, bound as an analysis-spec parameter ...)")
docs/coop/design-corrections/foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-payload-registry/law/unregistered ("a key with no row refuses; there is no default row and no caller-selected schema")
docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/identity-and-evidence.md section 3 payload registry table, class `parameter`: "a document on the closed list; today only foundation/import-source-context.schema.json"
newMustIssues.observation: An analysis-spec parameter row is `{schemaDigest, payloadDigest}` whose payloadDigest is resolved through the `parameter` payload class keyed by schemaDigest. That class is closed to one document. A ScopeDocumentV1 parameter therefore refuses at Plan admission, so the comparison contract's own scope axis cannot be populated.
newMustIssues.whyItIsAMust: One contract requires a binding a sibling contract's closed registry forbids. The comparison scope axis (E2 to E3) is unimplementable as written.
newMustIssues.requiredCorrection: Add the ScopeDocumentV1 row (document plus selector) to x-opensip-payload-registry.classes.parameter.rows, or move the scope-policy document out of the analysis-spec parameter mechanism and name its actual carrier.

newMustIssues.title: The required partial-ownership Coverage disclosure has no publishable typed cause
selectors: docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/identity-and-evidence.md, `clones` section: "the clones scope mints no body identity, its Coverage reports the incompleteness, and the predicate and seal are indeterminate rather than a false pass"

docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/native-evidence.md section 10, row `input-closure-incomplete` (closed cause list: missing-dependency-source, lockfile-missing, source-replacement-outside-snapshot, generated-output-unavailable, generated-file-missing, generated-file-out-of-bounds, no-program-unit, node-modules-outside-read-set, config-flag-stripped)
newMustIssues.observation: The three refusable ownership states named by the languageVersionBinding selectionLaw (BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNERSHIP_REQUIRED, BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_UNENUMERATED, BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_AMBIGUOUS) must surface in the clones Coverage entry as a typed deficiency plus nativeCause. No NativeCause member names any of them, and the section 10 row that would carry them enumerates causes that exclude them.
newMustIssues.whyItIsAMust: The contract mandates a specific public disclosure and the closed vocabulary cannot express it. Every implementer must invent the pairing, and the CLI/JSON/SARIF/HTML/agent parity fields would then differ between implementations.
newMustIssues.requiredCorrection: Add the ownership causes to NativeCause and to the section 10 input-closure-incomplete row (or give them their own row).
newMustIssues.reconstructionImpact: RUN-RUST-PARTIAL uses deficiency=input-closure-incomplete with nativeCause=null as a stated assumption; nativeCause is nullable so the record validates, but the disclosure carries no cause.

newShouldIssues.title: A record and its claimed 'exact mirror' declare different owning array orders for the same digest preimage
selectors: docs/coop/design-corrections/workflows/schemas/imported-evidence.schema.json#/$defs/ImportWrapperV2/properties/omissions (x-opensip-order: sequence; description claims 'Exact mirror of foundation import descriptor fields')
docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/identity-and-evidence.md section 3: "No caller may elect a different order for one schema"
docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/workflows-and-surfaces.md section 12: "The native and workflow import builders produce byte-identical wrappers"
newShouldIssues.observation: Under canonical-set the array must be strictly ascending; under sequence any order is admitted. An import whose omissions are ['b','a'], or a scope descriptor whose workspaceRoots are unsorted, is admissible through the workflow document and refused by the foundation document that owns the same digest preimage. The byte-identical-wrapper claim then fails for exactly the inputs the two schemas disagree about.
newShouldIssues.requiredCorrection: Make the mirrors declare the owning order, or state which document is authoritative and generate the other.

newShouldIssues.title: `import.blobs` cardinality diverges between the foundation record and the workflow mirror
newShouldIssues.observation: An import with zero blobs, or with more than 4096 blobs, is admissible in one unit and refused in the other, although importId is one H identity over one wrapper.
newShouldIssues.requiredCorrection: Reconcile minItems and maxItems, or declare one document authoritative.

newShouldIssues.title: `ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1.contentSha256` is described as snapshot-inventoried and as deliberately not snapshot-inventoried
selectors: docs/coop/design-corrections/native/native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1 description: "contentSha256 is the raw SHA-256 of that package directory manifest file bytes (its package.json) as inventoried in the snapshot"

docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/native-evidence.md section 2.2: "These rows are not snapshot inventory rows and must not be: the one shared discovery rule prunes node_modules by path segment, so the layout is a retained resolution observation of bytes the analysis read, joined by digest rather than by snapshot membership"
newShouldIssues.observation: The machine-readable registry resolves this in favour of the prose (a blobJoin, not a snapshotJoin), so I built the layout as retained blobs outside the inventory. The schema description still states the opposite and an implementer reading only the schema would add node_modules paths to the snapshot inventory, contradicting the shared discovery pruning rule.
newShouldIssues.requiredCorrection: Correct the schema description to match section 2.2 and the blobJoin annotation.

nonBlockingAdvisories.title: Pin-inventory completeness is not expressible in the closed disclosure schema
nonBlockingAdvisories.observation: A schema-valid strict subset of the active pins validates. Completeness is a host obligation observed under the exclusive purge lease.
nonBlockingAdvisories.standing: The contract states this itself (workflows section 12: 'A schema-valid subset does not satisfy that obligation'). Recorded as a limitation of the schema, not a defect.

nonBlockingAdvisories.title: `EnforcementValue` admits a stronger token than the measured truth table
nonBlockingAdvisories.observation: A test step declaring network=ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER validates against the schema; TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED is a host-side join against permission-truth-tables.v9. Correct by design, but the schema alone is not the guard, so a reader must not treat schema validity as an enforcement claim.

nonBlockingAdvisories.title: Inventory relations have no capability row
nonBlockingAdvisories.observation: `file`, `package` and `vcs-change` appear in the relation registry and in the capability-manifest relation domain, but no matrix capability row names them, so the matrix does not say which component produces them. This is what makes CB3-MUST-3 also reach `file` facts in a repository with no TypeScript or Rust unit.

nonBlockingAdvisories.title: The 723-byte edition-map illustration is not reproducible from the published grammar
nonBlockingAdvisories.selector: docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/identity-and-evidence.md, `clones` section: "A Rust workspace of twenty-one crates already produces 723 bytes of raw map, against a maximum of 255"
nonBlockingAdvisories.observation: My own 21-crate edition map canonicalizes to 391 bytes under C. The design conclusion holds under my measurement (391 > 255, so the map cannot be a u8-length-framed frame component), but the specific number depends on unstated crate names. Treating it as an oracle would be wrong; I did not.

algorithmFreedomCorrectlyLeftOpen: Query planning is explicitly an optimization whose result must agree with a retained full scan (identity section 4). That is freedom, not a gap.

The L1..L3 normalizer itself: the contract requires retained preimage custody plus framed-identity checking and explicitly declines to grade tokenisation. FACT-IDENTITY owns level specifications; their absence from this kit is a scoped deferral, not a missing public contract, because normalisationVersion pins whatever bytes are used.
Near-clone grouping (Jaccard over 5-gram shingles), suffix-array or hash strategies, cache eviction, and provider process management are implementation choices.
SQLite WAL settings, fsync ordering and process-death handling are named as implementation qualification obligations, not design alternatives.

reconstructedChain.0-discovery: security S3 selects the authority root (config > vcs-default > cwd-default) over O_NOFOLLOW lstat/ACL custody, exports AdmittedBoundaryInventoryV1; native section 1.4 consumes it unchanged and derives WorkspaceUnitV2 per language family; the shared rule in discovery-defaults prunes node_modules/.git/target by exact segment.
reconstructedChain.1-typed-config: admission section 1.1 layers compiled defaults, global, project, interactive local and flags; the resolved semantic configuration always carries all five sections and a complete analysis.budget; resolvedConfigDigest is raw SHA-256 of its canonical bytes.
reconstructedChain.2-source: snapshot2 over ProjectId, sorted source inventory, resolvedConfigDigest, scopeDigest and vcsDigest.
reconstructedChain.3-operational-lifecycle: RequestId minted before admission; a fresh ExecutionId per admitted attempt; StepId is the zero-based DAG position; none of these enters a semantic identity.
reconstructedChain.4-native-context-and-universe: admit_native_context binds the language's context to retained closures; bind_typescript_universe / bind_rust_universe bind the universe to the exact admitted context bytes and the retained nested records; both re-run at Run closure over retained bytes only.
reconstructedChain.5-plan: plan2 over snapshot, capability manifest, semantic closures, analysis spec, resolved config, the SET of selected native context bare-hex digests, imports, policy, waivers, scope, budget and semantic grant.
reconstructedChain.6-facts-coverage-view: the host mints fact2 from an adapter-normalized C payload; admit_coverage_result_v3 mints coverage2 only from the host's own scope2, checking the provider's in-band subjectScopeCommitment against a value it never supplied; view2 joins scopes, facts and Coverage under one Plan and producer.
reconstructedChain.7-proof: the pure evaluator consumes only Plan-bound admitted inputs; each predicate proof addresses a node of the admitted RuleProgramV1 by the total address grammar (p, p.i, p.0) and names a retained witness; the host independently replays the whole normalized result before sealing.
reconstructedChain.8-evidence-seal-run: evidence2 may include proof2; seal2 includes both; run2 includes the seal. The graph is acyclic and I checked the direction rather than assuming it.
reconstructedChain.9-durable-receipt: closure validation and replay, then blob publication with fsync, then one synchronous ledger transaction carrying the Run manifest, object references, retained availability generation, pins and a commit receipt binding ExecutionId and the commit-inventory digest, then acknowledgement.
reconstructedChain.10-availability: sealed assurance (verified/verifiable/replayable) is immutable; current availability is a separate monotonic-generation record (retained/partial/expired/purged/corrupt/unavailable) and a query reports both.
reconstructedChain.semanticVersusOperational: Semantic identities are content-derived and exclude wall clocks, PIDs, RequestId, ExecutionId, credentials, authorization nonces, receipts and output destinations. Operational authority (grants, consent, leases, receipts) lives outside every content identity: RepoExecutionGrantV2 and RepairApplyAuthorizationV1 are referenced operationally and never enter Plan; only their semantic projection (principal kind, closure, owner-source digest, operation set, scope) does.
reconstructedChain.mutationVersusAnalysis: analysis and verify are the only steps that seal or link a run2. comparison, query, render, import, repair-preview, repair-apply, test-execution, native-preparation, mutation, export-delivery and doctor mint no Run.

limitations: Every OS, compiler, provider, cryptographic and SQLite observation in this reconstruction is a synthetic assumption stated as such. Nothing here measures a real toolchain, proves confinement, or qualifies a platform, a normalizer, an enumerator or a carrier.
I built descriptor graphs and admission logic, not a product. Passing my own reconstruction proves that the design is constructible under my reading; it does not prove my reading is the author's.

I did not read any author reference implementation, fixture, golden, report, prior review, or any other /tmp/opensip-design-corrections directory. Where an embedded example appeared in a normative document I treated it as illustration and computed my own vector instead.
The claimed parentSubjectSha256 was not verifiable from this kit; I verified per-file custody only.

Schema validation used the kit's own documents through a pinned local registry with no network. It establishes shape conformance, not semantic conformance: the joins the prose requires (snapshot joins, closure joins, frame re-admission, citation closure, budget agreement) I implemented and exercised myself, and my implementation is my reading.
I did not construct a `syntax-only` Run (CB3-MUST-3) and I avoided any policy needing a resolved or type minimum resolution (CB3-MUST-2). Both omissions are reported rather than worked around.
This review grants no readiness grade, no acceptance, no implementation authorization and no claim of product qualification.
